author: GamingBolt
description:
If Agent 64: Spies Never Die proves anything, it's that nostalgia can only really carry an experience so far. But in this case, it's far enough, with the mission and level design coexisting well with the more archaic elements. 

As an homage to a shooter that defined a generation and Bond games for many years to come, it can be enjoyable, and should offer more than enough content for anyone who really wants to earn their 007 status – I mean, 64 Agent stripes.
title: Agent 64: Spies Never Die Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls is finally here, and we’ve been putting all three versions of the new fighter through their paces to see if one platform manages to edge the others out regarding the game’s visuals and performance. Judging the differences has been difficult. Furthermore, the PC version’s performance complicated matters, especially since community reports did not match our own experience. However, like the Avengers we persevered, and have brought you everything we’ve seen and thought as we took on great fights in stunning stages. 

We were delighted with animations and an art style that feels just like watching a comic book in action, the outcome of the scene dependent on how good a beat-down you could dish out at a smooth 60 FPS. The news is all mostly good, but the little bit of bad should concern you if you’re looking at this one on PC. Join us as we tell you what’s up with this one.
title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Is Great on PS5 Pro and PS5, So What’s Going On With PC?

author: GamingBolt
description:
Maybe the real appeal of not subscribing to the “bigger is better” philosophy is that Mortal Shell 2 can focus on providing a unique, engaging experience in every aspect that matters. 

Either way, we won't have to wait long to find out since it launches on August 20th for Xbox Series X/S, PS5, and PC. Whether the spirit of FromSoftware courses through, or it turns out to be something else entirely, Mortal Shell 2 certainly has our attention.
title: Mortal Shell 2 Understands That Bigger Isn’t What Makes an Open World Better
